source.work: Gulru Necipoglu, ed., The Topkapi Scroll: Geometry and Ornament in Islamic Architecture; Mohammad al-Asad, The Muqarnas: A Geometric Analysis

sourceClaims.tierRule: a row is a tier of adjacent single units of equal height, often accompanied by bipeds at the same elevation
sourceClaims.levelCode: dotted star-surrounding units belong to the lower of two adjacent tiers
sourceClaims.workedHeightChoice: one common height for all tiers, equal to twice the depth of units in the uppermost row
sourceClaims.heightFreedom: a different height, or heights, for the tiers would be equally correct
sourceClaims.projectionInvariant: each row retains its plan location and is shifted only along the height coordinate

formalization.planCarrier: P=(K,S,L,B), with cell complex K, scaffold S, level marks L and boundary data B
formalization.heightCarrier: H_P, the source-admissible tier-height assignments for P
formalization.sectionLaw: pi(R_P(h))=P for every h in H_P
formalization.sourceWitness: H_P is non_singleton because the worked common-height choice and at least one different height or height assignment are both declared correct

relationToDrawing108.transferRule: the catalogue_5 compiler is a family_level hypothesis for drawing_108 until drawing_108_specific tier decoding or an extant realization is supplied

currentVerdict: Catalogue drawing 5 establishes a source-native many-to-one plan-to-geometry lift and a regular-core/irregular-boundary transition. It does not establish a macro-collapse defect or nonassociative physical action.
